item.title: Kyle Farmer’s 2026 Season: A Short Stint With Big Wasted Potential
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Farmer spent most of 2026 on the Atlanta Braves roster, yet he barely touched the field. The veteran infielder arrived in early February hoping to help his hometown club, but his time in the big leagues was short and quiet. He played only 14 games all season, a number that shocked fans who expected him to be a key backup. His path from signing to release tells a story of missed chances and a roster that simply did not need him. The Braves brought him in as a free agent in early February 2026, only to cut him and re-sign him a month later in March. Per Battery Power , he was meant to be an end-of-bench option who could fill in at shortstop or catch in an emergency. Instead, he sat on the bench for weeks, saw limited action, and landed on the injured list by mid-May. When he returned on July 4, he got just one plate appearance before the team released him on July 21. He signed a minor league deal later and came back in September, but his season was already over. A Roster Spot That Went Unused Farmer made the Opening Day roster, but that spot meant little when he could not get into games. He played ten games over six weeks and got only 15 plate appearances. His return in July lasted two games with one at-bat before he was let go. Even his late-season call-up in September brought just two games and three more plate appearances. In total, he slashed .222/.211/.278 with a 25 wRC+, numbers that show he could not hit at all. He finished with -0.1 fWAR, marking his second straight season below replacement level. On April 30, acting as the designated hitter at home versus the Detroit Tigers, he made his single start. He went 1-for-3 in that game, which was his best moment of the year. That single in the second inning helped score the first run, giving him a win probability added of 0.03. Per Battery Power, it has been two years since Farmer actually provided any value to a team. It was a tiny spark in a very dark season for a player who has played 97 or more games every year since 2019, except for 2020. Why The Experiment Failed The Braves hoped Farmer would be a safety net if Ha-Seong Kim got hurt, but the plan fell apart. He spent 2025 with the Colorado Rockies and had a terrible year with a -1.0 fWAR in 300 plate appearances. That bad season hurt his reputation before he even put on a Braves uniform. The team needed someone who could hit or play great defense, and Farmer did neither in his tiny sample. He played third base, second base, and shortstop but did nothing to stand out in any of those spots. At 36 years old, Farmer is past his prime, and the stats prove it. His career has been built on playing a lot of games, but he could not do that in 2026. The team gave him a chance to return to Atlanta, but they did not give him a real role to fill. He was supposed to be a utility guy, but he ended up being a bench warmer who got released in July. The numbers show he was not ready to help the team when they needed him

item.title: Caitlin Clark reacts to encouraging Jack Campbell news
item.description: Oct 1, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) walks on the court during the fourth quarter of game three of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs against the Las Vegas Aces at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images Many football fans have been keeping an eye on the story of Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered a frightening neck injury during Sunday’s game. Caitlin Clark has added incentive to monitor Campbell’s progress. Not only are she and the 2025 All-Pro both Iowa Hawkeyes, but Campbell’s wife Megan played with Clark at Iowa during the 2020-21 season. On Wednesday afternoon, after Campbell announced he had full movement in his lower extremities and was “continuing to make progress” with moving his upper body, Clark sent a quick message of support to her former teammate. On her Instagram story , Clark shared ESPN and Adam Schefter’s post featuring Jack Campbell’s statement. Underneath it, she commented three blue hearts and tagged Megan. Once a Hawkeye Megan Campbell (née Meyer) was a star high school player in Mason City, Iowa before joining the Iowa program in 2019. In 2020-21, she was a key contributor off the bench while Clark became the team’s freshman sensation, scoring 26.6 points per game and leading the Hawkeyes to the Sweet 16. While Meyer transferred to Drake following the season and enjoyed a stellar 2021-22 campaign, she and Clark obviously still have a connection, judging by the latter’s social media post. ‘Optimistic’ Campbell working toward recovery Jack Campbell went down while making a tackle in the fourth quarter of the Lions’ win over the Minnesota Vikings. The 26-year-old linebacker lay motionless on the field for several minutes before being immobilized and taken off on a stretcher. The Lions had been vague on specifics regarding Campbell’s condition, only saying Monday that things were trending positively. Campbell himself provided the details in a statement earlier today. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better,” he said. “My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.” The post Caitlin Clark reacts to encouraging Jack Campbell news appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Purple wave, blue wave: Valkyries parade doubles as election celebration
item.description: Valkyries' mascot Violet waves to fans in attendance to see the 2026 WNBA Champions at Jack London Square in Oakland, Calif. on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Following the ceremony, the team will bring the WNBA Championship Trophy across the Bay to San Francisco for the parade. (Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle) Giddy energy from Tuesday night's Democratic electoral sweep seemed only to grow Wednesday morning as revelers gathered for the Valkyries WNBA championship parade. That much was clear from the sign that Serena Poon held aloft as she stood on the ferry lawn at Jack London Square, where the players and their entourage would soon depart by boat to San Francisco. "Purple wave 10/31; Blue wave 11/2," it said, linking the team's come-from-behind victory on Halloween night to a national blowout by Democrats, one so overwhelming that pundits ran out of tidal metaphors to describe it. The connection seemed fitting when a procession of Democratic politicians strode down the Embarcadero to welcome the Valkyries players when their boat was set to dock near the Ferry Building at noon. Among the delegation: Sen. Adam Schiff, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, state Sen. Scott Wiener (who is now leading in the race to succeed Pelosi) and Mayor Daniel Lurie in a violet shirt. For Poon, the political contact high was palpable. "We're just riding the high of Valks win, and then last night was just historic with blue wave," she said. "It was like a blue tsunami, and I'm just so stoked." Every Embarcadero-bound BART train and Muni bus became a purple and black menagerie as fans flocked in with jerseys, feathery boas and birdlike headdresses. If the attire seemed apolitical, the placards were not. Beth Jaeger of San Francisco arrived at the Embarcadero at 8 a.m. dressed as a Valkyrie, complete with purple face paint - and a sign that said "In a world of Sophies, be a Gabby." The slogan referenced public comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has insisted that trans women should be barred from the WNBA. Henry, from Oakland, holds a sign celebrating both the Valkyries' championship and Democrats' sweeping wins in Tuesday's midterm election. (Saul Pink / S.F. Chronicle) On the back of Jaeger's sign: "Welcome to the Gay Area." Others echoed pro-LGBTQ messages that, while not directly tied to an election wedge issue on Tuesday, generally defied the Trump Administration's stances on gender politics and diversity. As the morning wore on, "Gay Area" logos proliferated along the Embarcadero: in shimmery ink on card stock, emblazoned on T-shirts, embroidered on denim jackets, scrawled onto decals. "It was already so hopeful to see them win, and then to see and then to see so much hope across the country," said Cat De La Pena of San Jose, dangling her own hand-made "Gay Area" sign with a portrait of Valkyries forward and championship MVP Gabby Williams, arms outstretched to sink a 3-pointer into the basket. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he’s needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster. Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team’s active roster. A player’s current club can’t block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it’s the player’s decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he’s released, he’ll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. A practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.

item.title: Dianna Russini reportedly returning to sports media ‘next week’
item.description: Credit: The Dan Patrick Show Dianna Russini has apparently kept herself on the sidelines long enough. The former top NFL insider for The Athletic who became embroiled in scandal this offseason after numerous photos surfaced showing her cozy and seemingly intimate relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is set to return “next week” according to a report by Mike Florio in Pro Football Talk . “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work ‘next week,'” Florio reports, indicating that it is “unclear” for what outlet she’ll be working for, or what job she will be doing. Russini resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after the New York Post published the first batch of photos showing her and Vrabel together at a high-end resort in Arizona. In her letter of resignation, Russini maintained that there was no foul play between her and Vrabel. “Rather than allowing this [scandal] to continue, I have decided to step aside now – before my current contract expires on June 30. I do so not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career,” Russini wrote at the time. Last month, the New York Post reported that Russini had hired crisis management expert Melissa Nathan , one of the first signs that the veteran NFL reporter was eyeing a return to media. Russini has not made any public statements since her resignation in April. Whether Russini will return in a capacity that relies on her credibility as a reporter, or in a role that is more personality-focused, is unclear. No doubt, Russini maintains a large rolodex of contacts throughout the league, though those sources’ willingness to speak candidly with her might be compromised after the scandal. Russini has long been able to hold court in more casual settings, however, and would likely command an audience even without dishing out NFL scoops. item.title: Valkyries star Gabby Williams reveals Michael Jordan reached out to her after WNBA championship win
item.description: Valkyries star Gabby Williams reveals Michael Jordan reached out to her after WNBA championship win originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michael Jordan knows a thing or two about winning, and Gabby Williams was in for a surprise of a lifetime when he reached out to congratulate her. The Golden State Valkyries star defeated the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, the first time that the league was pushed to the last qualifier round in the series. Williams, a forward for the Valkyries, shared that Jordan reached out to her to congratulate her on her first-ever WNBA championship win. “My Jordan rep agent texted me, and he was just like, ‘Just so you know, it’s not spam, but you’re gonna get a text,’ ” Williams told People about the moment. “And I was driving, and I was like, ‘Do not crash your car, do not crash your car. Get to the gym, get to the parking lot.’” Williams added that the six-time NBA champion praised her for becoming a WNBA champion. “He congratulated me, and said it’d been an amazing season and just told me, ‘Stay hungry.’ ” she told the outlet. “That felt like a very Michael Jordan thing to say.” Williams also left with the WNBA Finals MVP title after the thrilling 68–63 Game 7 victory over the Dream. She also praised their head coach, Natalie Nakase, for leading the team to the franchise's first-ever win. "Coach Nat is the most competitive person I've ever met in my entire life. But she is competitive in everything that she does, you know, even how she treats people, even how she shows up every day, and we all feed off of that," Williams said. "I think she's a leader by example. She cares so, so deeply on a human level for each person, and you just want to go through a wall for her." item.title: Brewers Should Avoid Signing Jake Bauers To Multi-Year Deal
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers Jake Bauers had a breakout season at 30 years old, and the Milwaukee Brewers extended him the qualifying offer. If Bauers accepts his one-year, $23.15 million offer, the Brewers don't have any choice to make. He will be back at that price. However, after the year he had, he should have a couple of multi-year offers on the table as well. The Brewers do not need to be one of the teams making one of those offers. Having Bauers back for one season would be great, because if he is unable to replicate his career year, they would be clear of him. There is a chance that his 2026 season ends up being something like Trent Grisham's 2025 season. Every team will need to decide whether they believe Bauers has finally figured out the big leagues with his new approach to the game or if last season was a fluke. The rest of the league may let the Brewers be the team that has to figure it out by making Bauers accept the qualifying offer. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? item.title: As Greg Schiano’s future hangs in balance, Rutgers fans have minds made up: ‘We need a change’
item.description: SHI Stadium was half-empty as Rutgers hosted a Big Ten blueblood, but those who made the trek to Piscataway made their voices heard. There were loud, sustained boos following a controversial call from the officials. There was a jubilant celebration as the final minutes of a close game ticked off the clock. There were frequent chants to fire an underperforming coach. The problem for the Scarlet Knights : all of that noise came from the visiting Michigan fans. Along with a 28-21 win on the field , the Wolverines (5-3, 2-3) blew out Rutgers (2-6, 1-4) in the stands on Saturday. Michigan fans made up at least half of a crowd that was announced at 39,540, the lowest official attendance at SHI Stadium for a non-COVID Big Ten game since head coach Greg Schiano returned in the 2020 season. Despite their team stumbling through a mediocre season, Michigan fans brought plenty of life into a moribund building. Rutgers fans, meanwhile, spoke with their absence. “I really don’t worry about things I can’t control,” Schiano said following the game. “I have enough of my own issues that I have to work on. I just try to do that. As I’ve always told you guys, I’m grateful for the ones that came, because those people, they’re supporting us through thick and thin. We’ve had thick here and we’re a little bit thin right now.” Two years removed from reaching a second straight bowl game and appearing to be on an upward trajectory, the Scarlet Knights are barreling toward their worst record of Schiano’s second stint after going 5-7 last fall. item.title: Dianna Russini finally returning to sports media after Mike Vrabel scandal
item.description: Next week will mark the halfway point in the NFL season, and apparently, also the return of Dianna Russini to sports media after she stepped down from her role with The Athletic in the wake of the scandal involving her and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that dominated the offseason. “Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards,” The Athletic’s Mike Semel, who conducted an internal investigation, said of the controversy. “Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed.” According to Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio, a “source with knowledge of the situation” has made it known that Russini has made it clear to people around the league that she’ll make her return “next week” The news comes after Russini reportedly hired infamous publicist Melissa Nathan, a veteran of multiple infamous Hollywood imbroglios, but one who isn’t without her own controversy, as she is facing perjury allegations due to her involvement in the incredibly messy situation between Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni. Many prominent figures across sports media also anticipated that Russini’s return to sports media was imminent. In August, Mike Silver sang her praises and predicted her return. “Really good friend of mine,” he said of Russini. “Worked with her at The Athletic for too short of a time, unfortunately. Really, really proud of the journalism we did together and honestly just really bummed that we don’t get to continue it because we worked really well together. “I don’t think people understand the level of elite that she was performing at in terms of keeping in touch with the really important people around the league. And I don’t mean just agents and transactional, like players, coaches, owners, all of it, talking, having real conversations with them every day and really knowing what was going on and competing at a very high level. “I do miss having her a lot. Very bummed that it all imploded. She became a very high-profile person. I’m not a super judgy person. I would never comment on tabloid crap.” Silver then praised her family, and predicted that when she returned, it’d be in a role other than an NFL insider. “And I do think she’s going to be back, probably not as an insider, at least in the short term. But I think she’ll be back in this realm, probably talking about football and other things pretty soon,” he said. It would seem we’ll know immenently just what capacity she’ll be back in. item.title: Could Queen City Quarter become an everyday destination in Uptown Charlotte?
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets are part of an ownership group that purchased the former EpiCentre complex in Uptown Charlotte, now known as Queen City Quarter, for $27.5 million. The purchase price covers a property with an estimated value of nearly $100 million. Sports analysts consider the three-company venture well financed. Erik Spanberg, a reporter with the Sports Business Journal, noted that the acquisition follows earlier municipal approvals for facility upgrades. “I don’t think many of us knew that the Charlotte Hornets were going to be part of the buying group,” Spanberg said. He added that “it started when the city approved the arena renovations and the training center,” explaining that “teams want to surround their arenas and stadiums with things that they develop and own.” PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Former EpiCentre site Queen City Quarter undergoes major change Rick Schnall, co-owner of the Charlotte Hornets, hinted in May that broader developments were being considered alongside basketball facilities. “From the beginning, this project is more than it is not just about basketball,” Schnall said. “It’s about continuing momentum in Uptown Charlotte in the city of Charlotte and strengthening the Spectrum Center and the community around it.” Other NBA franchises have pursued similar arena-adjacent real estate projects. In 2015, the Sacramento Kings entered a joint venture to redevelop a plaza into 1 million square feet of space known as Downtown Commons, or DOCO, surrounding the Golden one Center. According to the developer, that project influenced $6.7 billion in new projects by 2022, while bringing 150 retail businesses, residential units, hotels, restaurants, and increased foot traffic to the area. Spanberg noted that multiple franchises have executed comparable development projects around their venues. “In the NBA, you’ve seen not only Sacramento, but you’ve also seen Milwaukee Bucks do it really well with the beer district. You’ve seen the Indiana Pacers do it recently,” Spanberg said. He added that the long-term challenge for such projects lies in sustained activity. “The question always is, can you do it to an extent where people want to come not just on game day, but every day,” Spanberg said. Similar developments are also underway elsewhere in North Carolina. A new entertainment district is planned in Raleigh surrounding the Lenovo Center. According to the Sports Business Journal , those plans feature thousands of housing units, dining areas, and an enhanced tailgating experience for Carolina Hurricanes fans.

item.title: Sabres Get Reality Check on Dylan Larkin Trade
item.description: Larkin Red Wings Getty The Buffalo Sabres are a good team that is trying to return to the playoffs after breaking a 15-year drought. That’s going to have their fanbase circling every big name that might be available in an effort to improve the roster, and that includes Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin. Larkin requested a trade after last season ended, but he still hasn’t been moved. At first, Larkin was playing for the Red Wings to start this season, but that has stopped — he’s now not expected to play until he gets traded. The calendar is into November, though, and Larkin hasn’t been moved yet. The Sabres aren’t on Larkin’s 10-team approved trade list, yet that hasn’t stopped speculation that he could still end up in Buffalo. That idea came crashing down on Wednesday when The Athletic’s Matthew Fairburn weighed in. Sabres’ Dylan Larkin Trade Update Fairburn didn’t hold back in breaking down the potential for a Larkin deal. First, he explained that he understands how the thinking can get here. “Trades are fun, especially in a league where free agency has become even more watered down over the years,” Fairburn writes. “So I get why people want to throw ideas around and play general manager. And I do think it’s fair to expect Kekäläinen to make a significant deal at some point this season. He’s circled around a few doozies this calendar year between Colton Parayko and Connor Hellebuyck.” Despite that, Fairburn isn’t convinced the Sabres and Larkin will come together. “That said, the idea of Larkin might be a non-starter,” Fairburn writes. “The Sabres have the assets to pull it off and have had conversations with the Red Wings about those assets. But Kekäläinen is the type to have those conversations about any big-name player who’s available. He wouldn’t be doing his job otherwise. Larkin would fill arguably their most glaring need for a No. 1 center and comes at a reasonable cap hit. But the Sabres are not on his expanded 10-team trade list . How much will that list have to expand before Buffalo ends up on it? Are the Sabres even a more attractive option than simply staying in Detroit? Yes, Buffalo ended its playoff drought, but that’s still just one year. Assuming he doesn’t want to go to a Canadian team, that leaves 26 teams. I wonder if the Sabres would get on the list if it got to 15 teams? Would it take 20? And how much more would the Sabres have to pay for the Red Wings to be compelled to move him within the division? All of those questions make me hesitant to get people too excited about the idea. I also think the Sabres should be wary about adding a player who essentially needs to be begged to come to Buffalo. item.title: 'The objective is clear' - Aston Villa send firm message to Manchester United as Unai Emery commits beyond 2029
item.description: Unai Emery Aston Villa - Getty Aston Villa have publicly confirmed that Unai Emery is committed to the club beyond 2029 after positive talks with chairman Nassef Sawiris, ending speculation over a move to Manchester United. The Spaniard has been strongly linked with replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, where Villa travel this weekend in need of a response to Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League defeat to Barcelona. Aston Villa confirm Emery commitment amid Manchester United links Villa have moved to end speculation over Emery's future, releasing a statement on Wednesday that confirmed a clear commitment beyond 2029 following talks between the manager and club chiefs. The 55-year-old has been strongly linked with replacing Carrick at Manchester United . According to The Telegraph, Emery is in advanced talks over a new deal at Villa, which would nip rumours of a move to Old Trafford in the bud. It would have cost United £20 million to release him from his current contract. Villa statement reveals details of key meeting Emery's impressive four-year spell at Villa prompted talks with Sawiris, president of football operations Roberto Olabe and director of football operations Damian Vidagany over his long-term future. In a very transparent statement, the club confirmed the meeting had produced "positive discussions", with their update reading: "Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project. "The meeting brought together Nassef Sawiris, the club's Chairman and Unai Emery alongside President of Football Operations Roberto Olabe and Director of Football Operations Damian Vidagany. Emery set to stay at Villa into the next decade "The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years. "The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements." Emery signed a five-year contract extension in May 2024, 18 months after joining, but he now looks set to remain in charge heading into the next decade. What next for Emery, Villa and Carrick? Emery will be at Old Trafford this weekend when United host Villa, whose 3-0 loss to Barcelona and draw with Fulham last Saturday leave them needing a positive result before the November international break. item.title: Everything Luke Fickell said after Badgers loss to Iowa
item.description: Wisconsin head coach Luke Fickell leads his team to the field before their game against Notre Dame Sunday, September 6, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Wisconsin Badgers were embarrassed 30-0 by the Iowa Hawkeyes in yet another rivalry game flop, as they fell to 5-3 on the season and 3-2 in conference play. It was a game where Wisconsin lost on every side and was awfully reminiscent of the team’s previous two losses to Iowa. Luke Fickell has now been outscored 124-16 in his four games at Wisconsin against Iowa. After the game, Fickell spoke with the media, outlining his frustrations and sharing his thoughts on the game. Here’s everything he said after the loss on Saturday. Opening Statement Well, that’s an old-fashioned ass whooping, and it doesn’t feel good. Were we prepared? Were we not prepared? We didn’t play like we were prepared today. They asked me if there were any positives, and I said I don’t know that I could find any positives in the way that we played, the way we performed. Yeah, they kept battling no matter what, but that’s a foregone conclusion. You have to do that. It’s, do you battle with the intent? Do you have the intensity to understand what it’s going to be like when you walk into this place and what you have to do in order to not just win, but make this a game? And we did none of that today. It’s very, very disappointing. I’m not sitting here saying I’ve got any answers for you. I’m not pointing any fingers at anybody because all three phases of the game, we were completely manhandled for 60-plus minutes. On why this keeps happening vs. Iowa… I don’t know. We made an overemphasis on it in the past, on the rivalry and what we needed to be able to do all of spring football and all of winter and all of fall. And then this year, it’s like, look, let’s make sure we understand, we respect the rivalry, but we don’t overdo something that is going to put us in a position where we play too emotional and can’t play 60-plus minutes.
